statement.text:
(a) For a given positive integer $g$, are there only finitely many L-space knots
of genus $g$?
A related but more general question is:
(b) Question (Hedden): For which knots $L \subset S^{3}$ are there only finitely many
knots $K \subset S^{3}$ with
$\widehat{\mathrm{HFK}}(S^{3},K) \cong \widehat{\mathrm{HFK}}(S^{3},L)$?

(c) In some special cases, one expects stronger results saying that a class of
knots is characterized by its knot Floer homology. We state 3 conjectures,
ordered by their strength.
(i) For a knot $K \subset S^{3}$, if
$\widehat{\mathrm{HFK}}(S^{3},K) \cong \widehat{\mathrm{HFK}}(S^{3},T_{2g+1,2})$, then
$K = T_{2g+1,2}$.
(ii) For a knot $K \subset S^{3}$, if
$\widehat{\mathrm{HFK}}(S^{3},K) \cong \widehat{\mathrm{HFK}}(S^{3},T_{p,q})$, then $K$ is an
iterated torus knot.
(iii) Conjecture (Ni): For an L-space knot $K \subset S^{3}$, if all roots of $\Delta_{K}(t)$
lie on the unit circle, then $K$ is an iterated torus knot.
